full_text:
## Follow on update 6th August

The following sets some context to the reasons why we are taking a slow, steady and perhaps overly cautious approach to the development and launch of Kabocha as a Kusama parachain candidate. 

_**Warning**, this is not a particulary exciting update, but for those of you who care about the processes and planning that goes on behind a new crypto project and why things may take a little more time than you'd like, this may be of interest. _

From the above: 

> The team that has proposed to manage the KAB chain once launched is Decent Partners. After understanding more about how they are able to do this with regards to maintaining a decentralized utility coin, they've requested more time to review the structure of the launch. 

## **Why (true) decentralisation matters**

Edgeware is one of the most (if not the most) decentralised on-chain governed blockchains in existence, an achievement initially achieved [via 2019's lockdrop](https://blog.edgewa.re/full-details-on-the-edgeware-lockdrop/) and subsequently compounded by the emergence of our small, but active community - aka those holders who decided to take a more active role in the network. 

Commonwealth Labs's decision to distribute 90% of the tokens at launch and only retain 6% of the supply had intended and perhaps unintended consequences for them. 

Namely it was wildly successful when it came to participation, but simultaneously opened to door to other large holders to emerge and for a new community to form who had the ability to mediate their own objectives.

The stated ambition was for Edgeware to be a protocol for _governance experiments _and on that point it has delivered, though maybe not in the way the team originally thought. In simple terms, Commonwealth launched Edgeware, but they do not control it.  You can see how this could be seen as both a feature and a bug depending on your perspective. 

This decentralisation has led to coordination challenges due to many stakeholders and no central lead team with an ability to unilaterally enforce their will, but in the end this also confers the project with unique advantages - many of which are not immediately obvious but will become more so with time.

## **Changing regulatory environment**

As many of you will be aware, the regulatory environment around crypto has been changing rapidly.

It has always been in flux, but recently we have seen an increasingly active environment not just in the US, but also in Europe and the UK (where [Decent Partners](https://decent.partners) is based). 

Right now crypto is still very much a wild-west, but this is changing fast as can be seen with the [UK FCA's treatment of Binance](https://www.fca.org.uk/news/news-stories/consumer-warning-binance-markets-limited-and-binance-group).

This regulatory oversight will only increase in the next 12-18 months to:

- Provide better protections to consumers/investors
- Give clarity for teams wishing to launch blockchain based projects
- As a path for the launch of CBDCs (Central Bank Digital Currencies) that will integrate more easily with the broader ecosystem.
- To ensure tax is collected where and when its due


For everyone hoping we will soon be living in Bitcoin citadels, that is not going to happen. Crypto is not going to replace the nation state nor fiat currencies, it will exist parallel to it as both a complement and as a sandbox to offer up alternative ways to organise, fund and relate to each other and the world around us.

## **What this will mean for crypto**

These changes will inevitably have profound impacts on the state of the ecosystem and there will be a slow and then rapid unwinding of many projects and exchanges who have adopted shall we say a more _adventurous_ approach to their activities.

Edgeware is among a handful of projects that is genuinely and undeniably decentralised in the practicalities of on-chain governance. 

With its active community treasury and proposal system, there is also a pathway for the community to discuss, debate and enact decisions that benefit the collective rather than any individual, team or investor. 

## **Hedgeware >>> Kabocha**

The Commonwealth team originally [proposed Hedgeware](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1415-kabocha-kab-a-ksm-parachain-from-edgeware?comment=3784 Kabocha update - warning, its not exciting, but should explain why we are taking a slow and steady approach to its development and launch.) as a conclusion of their [2020 roadmap](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/509-edgeware-2020-roadmap-discussion), ticking the box on launching a Canary Net into Kusama. 

The snapshot and distribution favoured their team, but with no guarantees as to the ongoing development and maintenance of the network an approach that was perhaps a little short-sighted. Hedgeware itself was also intended to be pretty much a copy/pasta instance of Edgeware, with no real cultural or technical differentiation- favouring the established narrative that Kusama was merely a stepping stone to the real prize - Polkadot. 

There was push back on these decisions and instead we proposed a 'fairer' distribution that favoured the community. whilst also evolving the cultural alignment with Kusama, which has developed to become a truly independent network and not just a testing ground for Polkadot. 

You can see the seeds of this alignment with the updated [New-Futures proposal](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1127-web30-dao-and-nft-launchpad-on-edgeware) and strategic partnership with [RMRK](https://rmrk.app) - the foundations of Kusama's artistic community and the project that recently caused the relay chain to be flooded with transaction requests, such was the demand for NFTs minted on the platform.  

![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/7d4a8263-4a8b-4b73-b821-21d0055f5861.1628173169541)
In the end we are focused on making Kabocha a network focused on long term success, that the Kusama community wants to see happen, not just a network that might promise a return due to initial hype and defi opportunities. 
## 
## **Experience is everything**

As noted elsewhere, [Edgeware's unique advantage](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1133-defining-edgewares-key-differentiators-benefits) is its fair distribution and the resulting battle scarred experiences in not theoretical, but **applied on-chain governance**. 

Thom's [recent post](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1504-a-venture-community-edgewares-existing-strengths-and-the-future ) extends this thinking:

> We have significant experience in organizing governance activities, written playbooks on community engagement, and milestone tracking. We have a set of experts in blockchain able to review proposals and grasp the worth of new endeavors. 

Every other Substrate chain has yet to fully grasp the in production challenges and issues that come when real and meaningful community governance happens. 

Of course they have more centralised teams and distributions, but given the shifting regulatory environment, this will also present major challenges as they seek to 'fully decentralise' decision making and governance, something that will be easier said than done. 

In the end everyone is after the same thing - a functional network token that gains actual use, rather than a speculative asset that may later face greater scrutiny. 

![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/66cdc491-1f65-482c-b3f4-bb97906463d0.1628235964539)
## 
## **Launching Kabocha **

Although we as a community have experimented with a range of funding proposals, Kabocha will be the first chain conceived, incubated and launched by Edgeware community members - and by far the most complex for various reasons.

After the crowdloan, the launching entity of Kabocha, Decent Partners will take over responsibility for complex things such as exchange listings - and therefore the legal and compliance responsibilities that come with that. 

To benefit from the true (and messy) decentralisation that Edgeware offers when it comes to future regulatory oversight, we will therefore be proposing Kabocha as a funding proposal, with Decent Partners providing the community with the_ network services _required to fulfil the desire to launch a network into Kusama. 

It will be up to EDG holders to discuss, debate and approve this proposal and as such provide a mandate to Decent to deliver the project. 

In return Edgeware will receive a large stake and governance voice in the network, this aligns everyone and ensures both networks can benefit from each others experience and resources. 

Decent will not take a stake in the initial Kabocha network - there will be a maintainers fund derived from the distribution that pools into a community treasury (as with Edgeware) and then we will submit referendum proposals via the network's on-chain governance, alongside any other interested parties. 

Our role is to be a steward of the network - setting the initial strategy and developing and launching proposals from a wide range of partners. 

As the Decent Partners label would suggest, we have been developing this network of partners for some time, which along with our extensive experience in Edgeware's governance should ensure a faster activation of the network.

The next update will be the Kabocha funding proposal which will contain all relevant  details as to the date of the snapshot, key network design principles and an introduction to the overall project culture.

And given that Kabocha will be a parachain on Kusama, it makes sense to move in unison with the Kusama experiment and test minimal assumptions as we go. From my perspective here is a rough draft idea about Kabocha:

# Kabocha (KAB)

Kabocha aims to be part of the early batch of parachains on Kusama, aligning with Kusama's energy, experimental ethos and multi-chain minimalist philosophy. It's purpose will be to expand the capabilities of governance and treasury in Substrate/Web3.

**No fixed treasury **Kabocha's treasury can only increase dynamically through community governance. 

**RnD funding** Kabocha will fund impactful RnD projects through treasury proposals, and give birth to Substrate pallets and spawn future chains. 

## Backlog of future proposals: 

**Voting gamification**
Kabocha can aim to have the highest quorum (percentage turnout) out of any substrate chain. It can do so by having a community of active participants, rather than just passive traders, guided by voting rewards and slashes. non voters will be slashed and go into a pool, where voters will be rewarded. 

**Treasury guilds** Enabling member's guilds that can propose to manage a portion of the treasury. Kabocha will play a role to advance governance development through rewarding and slashing voting turnout,.

**Pumpkin (Demurrage) NFTs** Experiment with demurrage, which is tokens that deteriorate in value unless it is re-shared. 

## Pallets: 

**x-token**- Will be on Karura's DEX
**bridges-pallet-common** will bridge to EDG
**governance** will have similar governance to EDG,, but treasury proposals will go straight to referenda.
**RMRK **will be an early tester of the RMRK pallet, and participate in NFT development on Kusama. 
**EVM/Ink**, once available and stable we can potentially include these pallets.

Kabocha is currently being tested on Chachacha test relay network. It will then be tested on Westend, before going into the the crowdloan process. Da

Hey all. 

Thanks for the patience on this update, Aug 3.

## Broad Scope
Things have been shifting rapidly in the Substrate ecosystem on potential for smart contracts on parachains - it's now looking more murky than first expected, and will take more time to resolve at Parity / Upstream of our tech stack. On the bright side, this gives us more time to get this right as the issue affects all parachains. 

On the technicals, Ramsey, who was contracted by the chains governance to study and develop a parachaining process, continues to make progress. These processes are general - making sure we have the knowledge and pieces to execute a specific parachaining when it is time.

His updates:
- Now testing on chachacha, a relay testnet using dev parachains.
- Loading collator node into a docker image.
- Experimenting with the distribution scripts so we're ready when we have the distribution.


## A shift in strategy
The team that has proposed to manage the KAB chain once launched is Decent Partners. After understanding more about how they are able to do this with regards to maintaining a decentralized utility coin, they've requested more time to review the structure of the launch.

Additionally, we're seeing this chain less as a 'incentivized testnet' and more a product of Edgeware's core strengths: funding projects that will accrue value to the chain in a variety of ways. The 'chain factory' model, I've called it previously.  As such, KAB is being given more freedom to pursue a concrete vision that will allow it to experiment with projects and technology that is more tailored for the KSM ecosystem, improving the results of it's crowdloan attempt. 

In short:
- Edgeware still builds vital proof that we have the talent to launch parachains.
- Edgeware will still receive a massive amount of KAB tokens for funding this development, adding to our public wealth.
- EDG holders and KSM-contributors will still participate as planned in the distribution.
- We will continue to improv

Hey all. 

Thanks for the patience on this update, Aug 3.

## Broad Scope
Things have been shifting rapidly in the Substrate ecosystem on potential for smart contracts on parachains - it's now looking more murky than first expected, and will take more time to resolve at Parity / Upstream of our tech stack. On the bright side, this gives us more time to get this right as the issue affects all parachains. 

On the technicals, Ramsey, who was contracted by the chains governance to study and develop a parachaining process, continues to make progress. These processes are general - making sure we have the knowledge and pieces to execute a specific parachaining when it is time.

His updates:
- Now testing on chachacha, a relay testnet using dev parachains.
- Loading collator node into a docker image.
- Experimenting with the distribution scripts so we're ready when we have the distribution.


## A shift in strategy
The team that has proposed to manage the KAB chain once launched is Decent Partners. After understanding more about how they are able to do this with regards to maintaining a decentralized utility coin, they've requested more time to review the structure of the launch.

Additionally, we're seeing this chain less as a 'incentivized testnet' and more a product of Edgeware's core strengths: funding projects that will accrue value to the chain in a variety of ways. The 'chain factory' model, I've called it previously.  As such, KAB is being given more freedom to pursue a concrete vision that will allow it to experiment with projects and technology that is more tailored for the KSM ecosystem, improving the results of it's crowdloan attempt. 

In short:
- Edgeware still builds vital proof that we have the talent to launch parachains.
- Edgeware will still receive a massive amount of KAB tokens for funding this development, adding to our public wealth.
- EDG holders and KSM-contributors will still participate as planned in the distribution.
- We will continue to improve the community fund amount - originally slotted for 20% of network launch tokens to fund ongoing maint and to award EDG treasury. That breakdown is still under development, and will come in the form of a formal proposal from Decent to Edgeware - a test of our chain-DAOs ability to form a funding agreement: KAB gets EDG to fund it's launch, EDG takes equity in the new network. 


## A thought on DOT
I believe this model will be helpful for executing a similar vision for the DOT slot, allowing a team to propose to manage the DOT parachain, giving EDG equity in that.  This is particularly necessary because of the aforementioned smart contracts on parachain issue, which will require EDG to remain a solochain to retain smart contracting abilities "for the foreseeable future," in the words of Parity contact Bruno.

(sidenote, i can't tag a response to your ID and name - assume its the same as me, that you had a different ID at the start? mine is mrbulb, but tags to rich).

> **Kabocha is a parachain and Edgeware is not. **So there will be differences in technical considerations and different things to test. 

Well, if the goal is for Edgeware to be bonded to Polkadot, then Kabocha is going ahead... seems like it's both a canary net and an Edgeware-incubated chain to me...

re Rich and Thom's above: Statemint is a common good parachain, which is different from Karura or Shiden, or other networks that are getting slots through crowdloans. The latter are generally launching with all their modules, though not all may be *on* at the beginning.

This lets the Kabocha codebase remain similar to the Edgeware codebase, so they could even build out of the same Github repo with feature flags ([see here where Drew has set up a feature flag for building the Beresheet binary from edgeware-node](https://github.com/hicommonwealth/edgeware-node/pull/314)).

> I don't see how any of that is relevant. 
Im just sharing the process being used by other substrate parachains as they bond to KSM and add in key modules via upgrades.

would this not be the approach we would take?
I don't see how any of that is relevant.

Following on from my comment above:

> This is a chance to build from first principles, adding things as we go, as they are needed. 
 
Hopefully everyone has seen [this post by Gavin Wood](https://medium.com/polkadot-network/the-launch-of-parachains-78188fcf024f) too - worth reading if not, which sets out the parachain process for Kusama that Statemine (the parallel equivalent of Statemint - a Polkadot parachain). 

> First, a _Shell_ parachain will be deployed to it, which was just approved by governance today. 
> The Shell parachain is an “empty” parachain — it produces blocks, but has no functionality beyond being upgradable. 
> It has no concept of user accounts, staking, governance or balances. It doesn’t even have the time-stamping module to understand “time”. 
> Instead, all it does is listen out for a message coming from the Relay Chain’s governance apparatus authorizing it to upgrade. 
> When such a message is received, the Shell parachain will allow itself to be upgraded to whatever new logic the Relay Chain has authorized

And then from [Altair's post](https://medium.com/altair-network/announcing-altair-centrifuges-kusama-parachain-d4cd7d328187) (Centrifuge KSM parachain)

> Altair will launch as an empty Shell on Kusama and a runtime upgrade will be performed shortly after to then enable accounts, balances, and governance, and more.

Wouldn't you say Kabocha is more of a Edgeware's parachain on Kusama than it is a canary net for Edgeware? I'm confused by this slightly and I think so will others be. 

When people think of canary net they think of Polkadot and Kusama which are each live relay chains with their own independent governance. The two differences here are:

1. **Edgeware has a lot of governance in Kabocha**. On first look people might think Kabocha is a competing chain.
2. **Kabocha is a parachain and Edgeware is not. **So there will be differences in technical considerations and different things to test. 


Kabocha is Edgeware's parachain on Kusama!
Correct- we would still use the testnet, and vet there before i goes up the ladder.

> I understand this sentiment, but if it is to be an incentivized testnet for EDG, it needs to have a technical similarity. Obviously this is open for community discussion, but the laboratory functionality would be lessened by this. 

We probably still need a non-value bearing testnet to test things that might genuinely break the chain though? Somewhere to run upgrades in public for a while before risking people's funds?  Not that we're really pushing the current testnet very hard most of the time.

To me, Kabocha is a space for pushing the boundary and doing more edgy things than we might do on mainnet, but perhaps not in the sense of actually doing things that might break the chain?

Kusama loves kabochas! 

I'm glad we went with Kabocha, it aligns with the Kusama theme, the energy is light and it will invite people to take part in the creative edge of possibilities.

Here's Kusama with a big Kabocha behind her: [https://i.pinimg.com/originals/95/fe/b8/95feb835550d02a1ec56d326925d4443.jpg](https://i.pinimg.com/originals/95/fe/b8/95feb835550d02a1ec56d326925d4443.jpg)

> It seems prudent to me to launch with the most basic chain possible - governance / treasury and add things as we need, or certainly in line with a specific strategy for the chain, rather than just copy/paste everything over simply because it's what EDG has right now.
- Rich

I understand this sentiment, but if it is to be an incentivized testnet for EDG, it needs to have a technical similarity.  Obviously this is open for community discussion, but the laboratory functionality would be lessened by this. As Raymond stated:

> the same code should run on both networks so upgrading both in parallel should be straightforward) 
- Raymond

> Not a lead dev on Hedgeware here
Removed that line :) Just wanted to give credit to folks who contributed to getting here.

> will the Agency focus on Edgeware while Decent focuses on Kabocha?
This is basically the plan. See the Stewardship section above:

"After launch, Rich's organization Decent Partners will be stewarding the protocol in a similar role to the Agency, while the Agency will focus on the core deliverables stated above: technology experiments, EDG equity in other networks, and maximizing the media and PR effects our incubating this chain."

The Agency will be involved on those three core points to ensure that EDG benefits from it's incubation of KAB.  Decent will lead biz dev and community building over there -  but EDG will maintain a large governance voice in the new network through its community fund.

 While we can't guarantee that KAB will not take on a life of it's own, the dual mech of 1:1 to EDG holders and the  ~10-20% Community Fund in my mind, aim to ensure that this remains a functional asset to the holders that funded it.

Great post [@Thom Ivy](/edgeware/account/jKauGVPCQkteGTDKuuNwhYhMBrj5QuytgybEC4A5cS4Bki5) - you've done a really good job of pulling this together.

There is one initial note on the above:

> In order to maintain both the EVM and Wasm contracting modules (as that is what EDG offers and benefits from testing of,) we will not be altering the decimal places, and we will keep the 18 decimal places, equivalent to EDG. This is because the EVM functionality requires it. 

It seems prudent to me to launch with the most basic chain possible - governance / treasury and add things as we need, or certainly in line with a specific strategy for the chain, rather than just copy/paste everything over simply because it's what EDG has right now. 

This is a chance to build from first principles, adding things as we go, as they are needed. 

If we load too much in straight off, we just end up creating restrictions and replicating a fixed mindset that is driven by as yet unproven assumptions. 

We should at least have that conversation first.

Not a lead dev on Hedgeware here - as with the 3.3.0 upgrade, I'm only helping with release engineering, pre-release bug fixes, and coordination between the different parties.

I'm interested in whether involved parties will be splitting their time between Kabocha and Edgeware - will the Agency focus on Edgeware while Decent focuses on Kabocha? What about core devs (the same code should run on both networks so upgrading both in parallel should be straightforward).
